subject: physics
title: Snap the Electron
summary: Photograph a hydrogen electron on its Bohr orbit with attosecond flashes from a space station, then zoom in on the matter waves of planets.
ncertRef: Section 12.4, Bohr model of the hydrogen atom
concepts: De Broglie waves: orbit n holds n wavelengths
The quantum number of a planet
learningOutcome: The student can find a Bohr orbit’s radius n²a₀, its speed v₁/n and its period, which grows as n³, and use mvr = nħ to show that a planet’s quantum number has dozens of zeros.

levels.title: Ring flash
levels.adds: Baseline: the allowed Bohr orbits have radius rₙ = n²a₀ with a₀ = 0.53 Å, and orbit n holds n matter waves (Ex 12.7; Example 12.3; §12.6).
hints: The orbit of level n has a radius n² times the ground orbit, a₀ = 0.53 Å.
The first excited state is level 2, the second is level 3. Orbit n holds exactly n matter waves, since 2πr = nλ.
Level 3, for example, sits at 3² × 0.53 Å = 4.77 Å, not 3 × 0.53 Å.

levels.title: Camera trap
levels.adds: New idea: on level n the speed is v₁/n and one lap takes T = 2πr/v, so the flash time fixes where the electron is (Ex 12.6).
hints: On level n the electron moves at v₁/n, with v₁ = 2.19 × 10⁶ m/s, round a circle of radius n²a₀.
One lap takes T = 2πr/v. Divide the flash time by T to get the laps done.
Drop the whole laps. The part of a lap left over, times 360°, is the angle past the gate.

levels.title: Twin atoms
levels.adds: New idea: r grows as n² and v falls as 1/n, so a lap takes n³ times as long as on the ground orbit: T ∝ n³ (Ex 12.6).
hints: T ∝ n³: one lap on level 2 lasts as long as 8 laps on level 1, and one lap on level 3 as long as 27.
Keep only the part of a lap left over, and multiply it by 360°.

levels.title: Powers of ten
levels.adds: Apply it: mvr = nħ holds for any orbit, so the quantum number of a moon or a planet has dozens of zeros (Ex 12.9; §12.6).
hints: n = mvr/ħ, with ħ = 1.055 × 10⁻³⁴ J s. Multiply m, v and r first.
Write n as a × 10ᵇ with a from 1 to just under 10. A zoom of ×10ᵇ leaves a waves in the window.
For the Earth: mvr = 6.0 × 10²⁴ × 3.0 × 10⁴ × 1.5 × 10¹¹ = 2.7 × 10⁴⁰ J s.

misconceptions: Bohr’s rule only works for hydrogen and never for a planet
The electron moves faster on higher levels
The radius of level n is n times the radius of the first orbit
The period grows as n², like the radius
Any radius is allowed if the electron has the right speed
